service_path.title: Service Path
service_path.description:
Path to the OData service (appended to Base URL).

Examples:
• OData V2: API_BUSINESS_PARTNER
• OData V4: api_fixedassetacquisition/srvd_a2x/sap/fixedassetacquisition/0001

Find available services:
• SAP API Business Hub: https://api.sap.com/
• Your system: /sap/opu/odata/IWFND/CATALOGSERVICE/ServiceCollection

odata_version.title: OData Version
odata_version.description:
OData protocol version for this service.

• auto: Automatically detect from $metadata (recommended)
• v2: Force OData V2 (legacy SAP services)
• v4: Force OData V4 (modern SAP services)

Learn more: https://www.odata.org/documentation/

entity_set.title: Entity Set
entity_set.description:
OData entity set to extract data from.

Entity sets are collections of entities (like database tables).
Examples: A_BusinessPartner, SalesOrderSet, ProductSet

The dropdown will load available entity sets from the service's $metadata.

query_options.title: 🔍 OData Query Options (Optional)
query_options.description: Configure field selection, filters, expansion, and ordering

select_fields.title: Select Fields
select_fields.description:
Choose specific fields/properties to extract (OData $select query option).

Leave empty to extract all fields.

Benefits of field selection:
• Faster extraction (less data transferred)
• Lower API costs on metered services
• Focus on relevant data only

Learn more: https://www.odata.org/getting-started/basic-tutorial/#select

filter_expression.title: Filter Expression
filter_expression.description:
Filter records using OData $filter query option.

Examples:
• Status eq 'Active'
• CreatedAt gt 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z
• Price le 100 and Category eq 'Electronics'
• startswith(Name, 'SAP')

Operators: eq, ne, gt, ge, lt, le, and, or, not
Functions: startswith, endswith, contains, length, tolower, toupper

Learn more: https://www.odata.org/getting-started/basic-tutorial/#filter

expand_properties.title: Expand Navigation Properties
expand_properties.description:
Include related entities in the response (OData $expand query option).

Navigation properties represent relationships between entities.

Examples:
• BusinessPartner → Addresses
• SalesOrder → Items
• Product → Category

Expanded data will be flattened into columns or separate tables.

Learn more: https://www.odata.org/getting-started/basic-tutorial/#expand

fetching_options.title: 🔄 Fetching Options
fetching_options.description: Configure how data is fetched from SAP OData API

fetch_type.title: Fetch Type
fetch_type.description:
How to fetch data from SAP OData API:

• Full Fetch: Extract all records every time
  - Reliable, always complete
  - Slower for large datasets
  - Higher API costs

• Incremental Fetch: Extract only new/changed records
  - Uses timestamp field filter ($filter)
  - Faster and cheaper
  - Requires incremental field and state tracking

Learn more: https://www.odata.org/getting-started/basic-tutorial/#filter

incremental_field.title: Incremental Field
incremental_field.description:
Timestamp field for incremental fetch (required for Incremental Fetch).

Used to filter records: $filter={field} gt {last_run_timestamp}

Common SAP field names:
• LastChangedAt / LastChangeDateTime
• ModifiedOn / ChangedOn
• CreatedAt / CreationDateTime
• SystemModstamp

The field must:
• Contain timestamps
• Be indexed for performance
• Update reliably on record changes

destination.title: 📥 Destination
destination.description: Configure output table and how data is loaded to Keboola Storage

output_table_name.title: Output Table Name
output_table_name.description:
Custom name for the output table in Keboola Storage.

If empty, the entity set name will be used.
Example: business_partners, sales_orders, products

load_type.title: Load Type
load_type.description:
How to write data to Keboola Storage:

• Full Load: Replace entire table on each run
  - Simple, always up-to-date
  - Good for small tables
  - No risk of duplicates

• Incremental Load: Append new data to existing table
  - Keeps historical records
  - Requires primary key for deduplication
  - Efficient for large tables

💡 Recommended combinations:
  • Full Fetch + Full Load: Simple, for small tables
  • Incremental Fetch + Incremental Load: Efficient, for large tables
  • Incremental Fetch + Full Load: For CDC scenarios

Learn more: https://help.keboola.com/storage/tables/#incremental-loading

primary_key.title: Primary Key
primary_key.description:
Field(s) that uniquely identify each record (required for Incremental Load).

Used by Keboola Storage to:
• Deduplicate records (upsert operation)
• Update existing records
• Maintain data consistency

Common SAP primary keys:
• Single field: BusinessPartnerID, SalesOrderID, ProductID
• Composite key: MaterialNumber + Plant, AccountID + FiscalYear

💡 Even with Full Fetch, primary key is needed for Incremental Load.

Learn more: https://help.keboola.com/storage/tables/#primary-keys

advanced_options.title: ⚙️ Advanced Entity Options (Optional)
advanced_options.description: Override pagination settings for this entity. Leave empty to use global defaults.

page_size.title: Page Size
page_size.description:
Override the default page size for this specific entity.

Leave empty to use the global default.

Adjust based on:
• Number of fields (fewer fields = larger page size)
• Data complexity (simple data = larger page size)
• SAP server performance limits

max_records.title: Max Records
max_records.description:
Override the default maximum records for this specific entity.

Leave empty to use the global default.
Set to 0 for unlimited.

Useful for:
• Testing specific entities
• Controlling large extractions
• Sampling data
